The district shall not be responsible for the dissemination， replication or alteration of information
or data input by any student or staff into any Generative AI tool or resource. Nothing in this
policy is intended to limit the district’s obligations under applicable law or regulations.
The district shall not be responsible for any unauthorized charges or fees resulting from access or
use of Generative AI tools or resources.
Delegation of Responsibility
The Superintendent shall develop procedures to implement this policy and may delegate to
his/her designee(s) the right to enforce this policy.
The district shall make every effort to ensure that Generative AI tools and resources are used
responsibly by students and staff. The effective integration of Generative AI into education
requires a collaborative effort between administration， teachers， staff， students and families.
The district shall inform staff， students， parents/guardians and other users about this policy by
posting on the district website and by other efficient methods.
The Executive Director of Technology will continually evaluate and authorize Generative AI tools
and resources used in district schools and programs for age-appropriateness， bias， privacy
protections， accessibility standards， student and staff safety， and data security.
The Board directs that only district-authorized Generative AI tools and resources may be used on
district computers and in district schools and programs. Staff shall consult the district’s list of
authorized Generative AI tools and resources prior to implementation in the educational
environment. Unauthorized Generative AI tools and resources may not adhere to required data
privacy， monitoring and security standards.15 U.S.C. 6501 et seqPol. 815Pol. 830.1
The district solicitor， in coordination with the Executive Director of Technology， shall evaluate new
and existing vendor contracts， collective bargaining agreements， and related agreements for
impacts related to district use of Generative AI.
Definitions
Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to computer systems and algorithms that mimic human
cognitive functions， such as learning， reasoning， problem-solving and decision-making. AI
encompasses a broad spectrum of techniques and methodologies， including machine learning，
natural language processing， computer vision and robotics， aimed at creating intelligent systems
capable of performing tasks autonomously or with minimal human intervention.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Literacy – the ability to understand， use and interact with AI
systems effectively， efficiently and responsibly.
Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) – an advanced subset of AI that can
generate new content from learned data and pattern recognition across various mediums such as
text， code， images， audio and video data.
Open-source AI – AI tools and resources that are built on publicly accessible platforms and use
and share data among all users who access the platform， both within and outside of the district.
https://go.boarddocs.com/pa/alen/Board.nsf/Private?open&login# 2/7
7/21/25， 9:53 AM BoardDocs® Pro
Guidelines
Instruction on AI Tools
The Board directs that students at all grade levels receive age-appropriate AI Literacy instruction
on the proper use of AI tools， encompassing fundamental principles such as the necessity of
proper human supervision， critical thinking and skepticism regarding accuracy. Such instruction
should aim to empower students with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the
increasingly prevalent presence of AI technologies in their academic and personal lives. By
fostering a culture of responsible and informed use， students will be better equipped to navigate
AI tools effectively while understanding their limitations and ethical implications.
If assignments allow or require AI use or specific tools， those tools must be readily available and
provided for each student.
To ensure access and student agency， the district will provide training for neurodivergent
students and English Language Learners to understand and utilize Generative AI tools and
resources for their learning needs.[8][22][23]
CIPA Compliance
The Superintendent or designee shall be responsible for developing procedures to address
student safety measures and to determine whether Generative AI tools and resources are being
used for purposes prohibited by law， Board policy or for accessing sexually explicit materials.[47
U.S.C. 2542][Pol. 81525][18 Pa. C.S.A. 590329][18 Pa. C.S.A. 631230][18 U.S.C. 225631][20
U.S.C.713132][47 CFR 54.52033]
The Executive Director of Technology shall ensure that the district’s Internet content and
message filters prevent users from accessing any AI website， tool or application that is capable
of generating obscene or pornographic material on both school district-owned devices and on the
school-provided Internet.[5][19][24]
FERPA Compliance
All teachers， administrators and staff are required to adhere strictly to the regulations outlined in
the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) when utilizing any AI resources.[1][10]
[25]
The district prohibits the use of personally identifiable information of students while using AI
websites， tools or applications that have not been pre-approved by the Executive Director of
Technology or his/her designee. The Executive Director of Technology shall establish an efficient
process by which teachers and administrators can request the approval of new AI resources. The
Executive Director of Technology or designee shall maintain a public list of all such approved
resources.
Ethical Considerations
The district shall prioritize the educational value in the use of Generative AI tools and resources
and will take measures to mitigate associated risks. The district shall only authorize Generative
AI systems and platforms appropriately equipped for preventing breach of personally identifiable
information and addressing the district’s prohibitions against discrimination， harassment，
bullying， bias and access to sexually explicit materials， or those which are harmful to minors or
prohibited by Board policy. [Pol. 113] [Pol. 103.1] [Pol. 104] [Pol. 249] [Pol. 815]
The district’s technology protection measures shall be enforced during use of Generative AI on
district computers and network resources.[Pol. 815]
https://go.boarddocs.com/pa/alen/Board.nsf/Private?open&login# 3/7
7/21/25， 9:53 AM BoardDocs® Pro
The district shall provide additional training， when needed， and address accessibility needs to
provide access to Generative AI tools and resources for students and staff including， but not
limited to， individuals with disabilities and English Learner students.[Pol. 103][Pol. 103.1][Pol.
104][Pol. 113]
Academic Integrity
The Board recognizes the capacity of AI to complete many student assignments. In doing so， AI
has the potential to upend traditional academic honesty and plagiarism standards. It is the
responsibility of the district to develop guidance on types of AI use and alignment to academic
integrity.
The use of Generative AI by students to complete assignments or assessments shall only be
allowed to the extent stated and outlined by the teacher for the individual assignment or course.
Students shall be notified in advance of the parameters for use of Generative AI in assignments
and assessments.
Students and staff shall receive training and be expected to appropriately cite original sources for
quotations， facts， information， statistics， dates or the paraphrased statements of others.
It is the responsibility of all students to appropriately cite content generated by AI when
generated content is quoted， paraphrased or otherwise used in the student’s work. Lack of
citation to AI generated work improperly implies that the work is entirely that of the student.[Pol.
218]
Having received such notice from a teacher， any student who violates these standards is subject
to discipline including， but not limited to， detention， suspension or expulsion depending on the
nature of the violation.[11][26][27]
Copyright
Individuals using Generative AI tools and resources must comply with federal law and Board
policy regarding the duplication or use of copyrighted materials.[17 U.S.C. 101 et seq][Pol. 814]
AI-Generated Content Verification -
Individuals using Generative AI tools and resources have a responsibility to apply proper
oversight and evaluation of generated information. Generative AI tools shall not be the sole
determining factor used to make decisions related to student learning， assessment， academic
integrity or conduct. Staff and students should critically evaluate content produced by Generative
AI for potential biases or inaccuracies and understand the importance of cross-referencing with
trusted resources.
Evaluation and Monitoring of Generative AI
Administrators， network supervisors and teaching staff shall establish processes for ongoing
evaluation and monitoring of Generative AI tools and resources used within the district and on
https://go.boarddocs.com/pa/alen/Board.nsf/Private?open&login# 4/7
7/21/25， 9:53 AM BoardDocs® Pro
district computers and network resources， including periodic assessments of the impact on
student learning.
Issues identified during the evaluation and monitoring process shall be reported to the District
Innovation Task Force.
Acceptable Use
The Board encourages students to leverage AI as a learning tool， when authorized by the
student’s teacher， to enhance their understanding， creativity and critical thinking skills. The
Board emphasizes responsible usage， proper attribution and clear guidelines to discourage
academic dishonesty， including the requirement to verify AI-generated information with reliable
sources.
All students and employees shall comply with the district’s policy on the acceptable use of district
technology when using AI tools on school district technology. Violations of the district’s
acceptable use policy may result in disciplinary action against the student or employee.[19]
Student use of AI tools while using district technology or engaged in district activities is also
governed by the Code of Conduct， which is hereby incorporated by reference.[11]
This policy shall also apply to student conduct that occurs off school property or during non-
school hours to the same extent as provided in Board policy on student discipline.[11]
Grading Student Work
Approved AI websites and applications may be used to assist with the grading of student work
products， but final decisions on assignment grades and evaluations shall be determined by
teachers and not solely by AI technology.[Pol. 103.1][Pol. 113][Pol. 114][Pol. 127]
Teachers shall ensure that personally identifiable student records are kept secure when using
such grading technology.[10][28]
AI Use in Operations
The Superintendent shall establish protocols to verify the accuracy and reliability of the output
from AI tools prior to the use of such tools for budgeting， payroll， financial or population
forecasting， HR analytics and similar operational tasks.
While AI tools may be used to assist in HR processes so long as the protocols above are in place，
the Board directs that final decision-making regarding employee evaluations， promotions and
hiring be human decisions and not solely by AI technology to ensure fairness， and compliance
with anti-discrimination laws.[9]
The district prohibits the use of Generative AI in making decisions regarding employee
recruitment， hiring， retention， promotion， transfer， evaluation， demotion or dismissal.[Pol. 104]
Professional Development
The Board directs the Superintendent to provide regular professional development training for
administrators， teachers and staff on the ethical and appropriate use of AI in school. The training
should equip educators， administrators and staff with the knowledge and skills necessary to
integrate AI tools into their roles in the district， while also addressing data privacy， legal

compliance and ethical considerations. Additionally， the professional development will
address access to Generative AI tools and resources for students and staff including， but not
limited to， neurodivergent students and English Learner students.[8][22][23]
Consequences for Inappropriate Use
Failure to comply with this policy or district rules regarding appropriate use of Generative AI
including， but not limited to， acceptable use of computer and network resources， shall result in
usage restrictions， loss of access privileges， disciplinary action and/or referral to legal authorities.

Students and staff must immediately report any violations or suspicious activity to the building

Illegal use of Generative AI， intentional modification without permission or damage to files or

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) (Central Bucks School District)
full_text:
Artificial Intelligence (AI)
At the Jan. 2， 2025 Education Committee meeting， members of CBSD's Technology and Innovation Department provided a comprehensive update on how our faculty and staff continue to study， provide training on， and thoughtfully explore the use of artificial intelligence as a productivity and educational tool in CBSD. The update included information on a draft of a district “AI Handbook;” upcoming professional development; and， most significantly， how the district is investigating ways to support students’ responsible use of AI， possibly beginning in the 2025-26 school year.
The PowerPoint can be viewed
here
and the presentation
here
(beginning at 51:57).
Careful and Thoughtful Consideration
Background on Exploration of AI in CBSD
Looking Ahead to 2026-27 and Potential Student Use
Questions or Comments
CBSD seeks to be forward-thinking about AI; our mission statement stresses the importance of life-long learning. Since ChatGPT launched in November 2022， perhaps no other subject has required such rapid learning across all ages than artificial intelligence.
At the same time， we wish to be deliberate and thoughtful about how AI might be utilized responsibly， ethically and strategically throughout our school system， including beyond the classroom in various administrative departments. Currently， with support and resources available from the district， our teachers and staff can utilize Microsoft’s AI assistant， Copilot， and the AI features built into the online graphic design tool， Canva. While our students also work in Microsoft and Canva， the AI tools offered by these services are not yet available to them.
Our goal with AI is to make informed decisions for the future and move forward with positivity about the possibilities while recognizing the necessary guardrails required should we support our students’ structured use of AI as an educational tool.
Less than a year after ChatGPT launched， in August 2023， CBSD formed an AI Committee of teachers， administrators， and staff to explore and discuss the potential impact of AI on the district’s teaching， learning， and general operations. Members of our technology and innovation team are uniquely positioned to help us chart a path for AI’s use in the district， including in the classroom. Several of them were or are teachers in addition to their expertise in technology， ensuring the department is well-versed in student learning needs， the dynamics of a classroom setting， and the logistics of academic assignments.
In February 2024， members of the department began attending conferences that included sessions on AI， and several team members also had the opportunity to present at a session. This past summer， the committee built on its work to draft an “AI Handbook” to aid our teachers and staff in understanding AI best practices and how AI might be used in the classroom. The handbook was shared with employees in late November and reflects the district’s belief in maintaining a human-centered approach to education – one that continues to emphasize the importance of student creativity， critical thinking， and integrity， while also considering AI’s potential as a tool to enhance learning.
This school year， stakeholders across the district have been further engaged in the AI conversation. Over the summer， choice professional development sessions on AI tools were offered. In October， administrative leadership received a formal update， and principals were briefed in November. This month， members of the administrative leadership team， teachers and staff will receive further training on Copilot. In February， our technology and innovation team will host additional professional development sessions for teachers， building on last year’s AI-focused district-wide professional development day， which centered on teachers using AI for productivity and lesson planning purposes. Finally， this summer， we plan to expand these efforts with further training sessions.
Currently， Microsoft Copilot and Canva AI are the approved tool for students. Students must be in a district-approved AI pilot to utilize Copilot. Teachers that would like to be considered to have their classes participate in the AI pilot should reach out to either a district staff developer or a member of the Technology and Innovation department.
As CBSD continues to investigate and plan for how AI could be
utilized
effectively，
ethically
and responsibly in district classrooms， the community will be kept informed about our progress.
As with all initiatives， feedback is welcomed at
information@cbsd.org
.

outlines the district's approach to integrating AI tools in our educational practices. The handbook was developed by a committee of teachers， administrators， and stakeholders to ensure that we navigate the evolving world of AI in a way that benefits our students， staff， and families.

shall evaluate new and existing vendor contracts ， collective bargaining agreements and related
agreements for impacts related to district use of Generative AI.[34][35]

INSTRUCTION ON GENERATIVE AI TOOLS
The board directs that， where applicable， students shall receive developmentally appropriate
instruction on the proper use of Generative AI tools， encompassing fundamental principles such
as the necessity of proper human supervision and skepticism regarding accuracy. Such
instruction should aim to empower students with the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the
increasingly prevalent presence of Generative AI technologies in their academic and personal
lives. Instruction shall emphasize critical thinking， responsible use， and awareness of the ethical
limitations of Generative AI tools.

The Director of Innovation shall make every reasonable effort to ensure that the district’s internet
content and message filters prevent users from accessing any Generative AI website， tool， or
application that is capable of generating obscene or pornographic material on both school district
owned devices and on the school provided internet.

the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) when utilizing any Generative AI
resources. Use of student information in Generative AI shall comply with FERPA and the
district’s Generative AI approval procedures established under this policy.

The Board recognizes the capacity of Generative AI to complete many student assignments. In
doing so， Generative AI has the potential to upend traditional academic honesty and plagiarism
standards. Generative AI is not permitted to be used on graded assignments or projects without
express written instructions from the teacher. Teacher shall It is the responsibility of all teachers

is permitted on a particular assignment or projectthe extent to which Generative AI may be used

written instructions from the teacherteacher permission to the contrary. Students who use

Student Code of Conduct.

shall remain the sole responsibility of the teacher to use their professional expertise to evaluate
and grade student work. Approved Generative AI websites and applications may be used to assist
with the grading of student work product， but final decisions on assignment grades shall be
determined by teachers and not solely by Generative AI technology. Teachers shall ensure that
personally identifiable student information and records are kept secure， in compliance with
FERPA， when using such Generative AI technology. [8][9][11][14][36][37]

the appropriate use of Generative AI， focusing on instructional integration， data privacy， legal
compliance， and ethics.

District Technology when using Generative AI tools on school district technology. Violations of
the district’s Acceptable Use Policy may result in disciplinary action against the student or
employee. [37] [38]
Student use of Generative AI tools while using district technology or engaged in district
activities is also governed by the Student Code of Conduct， which is hereby incorporated by
reference. [25]

Generative AI shall support， not replace， human judgment. Staff retain full responsibility for all
high-stakes， consequential decisions informed by Generative AI outputs， ensuring accuracy of
the information and/or output provided by Generative AI and that the decisions are fair， legally
compliant and aligned with district values.
The District directs that all decisions informed by Generative AI outputs and that impact
teaching or learning shall include meaningful human review and approval， including， but not
limited to， checking the Generative AI output for accuracy， potential bias， and legal compliance.
Generative AI outputs shall be treated as advisory information to support human users in making
informed， responsible， and contextually appropriate decisions.
Staff may use Generative AI tools to assist with research， organization of information， or
drafting; however， these tools must not be used to make， recommend， or substantiate decisions
regarding student discipline or personnel matters. All decisions must be made by staff using their
own professional judgment， and in accordance with District policy and procedures.
GENRATIVE AI USE IN OPERATIONS
The Superintendent or designee shall establish protocols to verify the accuracy and reliability of
the output from Generative AI tools prior to the use of such tools for budgeting， payroll， financial
or population forecasting， HR analytics， and similar operational tasks.
Employees shall not input confidential or personally identifiable district data into any Generative
AI tool unless explicitly authorized and approved through district procedures.

shall make all decisions regarding employee evaluations， promotions， and hiring.

procured Generative AI tools for effectiveness， compliance， and risk.

The board’s purpose of implementing a policy on Artificial Intelligence (AI) is to ensure the
ethical and responsible use of AI technologies to enhance teaching， learning， and

Delegation of Responsibility
The Superintendent or designee shall develop procedures to implement this policy and may
delegate to his/her designee(s) the right to enforce this policy.
Definitions
Artificial intelligence (AI) refers to computer systems and algorithms that mimic human
cognitive functions， such as learning， reasoning， problem-solving， and decision-making. AI
encompasses a broad spectrum of techniques and methodologies， including machine
learning， natural language processing， computer vision， and robotics， aimed at creating
intelligent systems capable of performing tasks autonomously or with minimal human
intervention.
Generative Artificial Intelligence – a subset of AI that can produce new content from a
sufficiently large data set across multiple forms of media.
For the purposes of this policy， AI does not refer to technology tools or subsystems
incorporated into systems or applications to improve basic functionality. Examples of this
could include intelligent monitoring of HVAC or security systems， automatic categorization
or new websites， grammar correction tools， or accessibility tools such as voice control. This
policy is intended to govern the use of generative or other advanced AI applications.
Guidelines
Instruction on AI Tools
The board directs that students at all grade bands--primary， intermediate， middle， and high
school-- receive age-appropriate instruction on the proper use of AI tools， encompassing
fundamental principles such as the necessity of proper human supervision， critical thinking，
and skepticism regarding accuracy. Such instruction should aim to empower students with
the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the increasingly prevalent presence of AI
technologies in their academic and personal lives. Instruction should be incorporated into
existing lessons on technology， media literacy， research skills， and academic honesty.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly become integral in daily life， and Texas K-12 students
and educators are navigating the opportunities and risks largely on their own. The Texas
AI in Education Task Force， a coalition of educators， administrators， higher education
professionals， industry leaders， parents， and nonprofit representatives， convened by the
Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) at The University of Texas at Austin， produced

THE CHALLENGE
Texas is one of only five states with no formal AI guidance for K-12 education， even though
student use has skyrocketed. Currently， only about a quarter of Texas school districts pro-
vide guidance for AI use for either teachers or students. This leaves students without the
guardrails needed to help them navigate AI appropriately. Continued inaction risks student
misuse， over-reliance on AI， harm to cognitive and social-emotional development， data
privacy violations， workforce unpreparedness， and uneven educational experiences across
1，200+ districts. This is particularly serious given the ubiquitous access to AI that today’s
students have outside of school. Because Texas is one of the largest public school systems
in the country， with roughly 1 in 10 U.S. K-12 students and 1 in 9 U.S. public school teachers，
this indecision has an outsized impact on student preparation for the entire country.
THE STAKES
The safety of Texas’ students is paramount and our children are exposed to AI embedded in
the technology they use every day in and out of the classroom. We need guidelines， literacy
frameworks， and professional preparation to support the responsible implementation of

needed now is the political will and investment to use it.

independent districts.

assessment. Guidance should also reflect the need for community and
family engagement in the creation and implementation of local policies.

The state should invest in a coordinated， hub-and-spoke initiative to
build AI literacy across all educators and administrators. The existing
Texas Computer Science Pipeline network should be expanded to address
AI safety， responsible use， and instructional integration as appropriate，
while building long-term capacity in educator preparation programs.

This generation of Houston ISD learners represents our greatest opportunity yet to instill the future-

As middle-skilled jobs shrink and higher-skilled roles become more prevalent， aptitudes like critical thinking， lifelong learning，
teamwork， information literacy， communication， and AI collaboration will be crucial to success in the workplace.1
By embracing cutting-edge technologies like generative AI， Houston ISD can empower students to develop proficiency in vital
2035 competencies. Responsible， safe， and equitable access to generative AI will open new avenues for personalized learning，
accelerated skills acquisition， and augmented creativity and problem-solving. Moreover， cultivating robust generative AI literacy
across our community will ensure our students graduate future-ready and well-equipped to thrive.
While this transition brings challenges， Houston ISD views it as a tremendous opportunity to transform education. With the right
strategies and support systems in place， our students can lead the way as resourceful， tech-savvy innovators and leaders in the
era of artificial intelligence.

the level of thinking—reducing time spent on first drafts and surface-level tasks so students and staff can focus on reasoning，

District Initiatives to Increase AI Literacy
FutureReady Cohort The FutureReady Cohort serves as the district’s foundational training initiative designed to equip all
(Staff) staff—including both campus-based personnel and central office employees—with the knowledge and
skills necessary to ethically and effectively integrate generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into
their daily responsibilities. The core purpose of the training is to improve personal and professional
workstreams by teaching participants how to use district-approved AI tools and apply best practices for
responsible GenAI engagement.
The grand overview of the cohort is rooted in the mission to prepare students for the future and
ultimately improve student outcomes by making it easier for adults to apply AI into their practice. This
journey requires all employees to continually adapt and grow their skills， with the program guiding staff
through an AI Competency Continuum toward a goal of reaching at least the “AI Navigator” stage. The
training ensures all staff understand the district’s overall AI strategy and implementation ， covering
critical areas such as defining GenAI， discussing its ethical implications， exploring use guidelines， and
prioritizing safety and privacy concerns.
HISD AI Competency Continuum
AI + CTE Pathways The core purpose of integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Career and Technical Education (CTE) is
(Students) to build AI literacy and cultivate future-ready skills across the modern workforce. Recognizing that
industries increasingly require AI competencies， the district’s strategy is to proactively build AI
readiness by embedding AI literacy and the use of AI-specific tools directly into CTE instruction. This
grand vision prepares students for future occupations by introducing tools that enhance key functions
across various pathways.
For instance， AI automates system monitoring and cyber threat detection in IT， optimizes traffic and
identifies intrusions in Networking， improves productivity and automates testing in Programming，
and enhances CAD design while supporting robotics in Engineering. Furthermore， AI assists in
diagnostic imaging and predictive analytics in Health， guides weld-quality analysis and facilitates smart
construction in the Trades， and drives individualized education program (IEP) drafting and real-time
translation in Human Services.
The overall goal is to ensure students， whether in the initial pilot pathways (Advanced Cloud Computing/
Fundamentals of Computer Science and Principles of Applied Engineering) or other future-integrated
pathways， are equipped with the skills needed as AI adoption becomes standard across industry sectors.
HISD will continuously refine AI integration in CTE pathways through ongoing feedback from industry
partners to ensure alignment with evolving workforce expectations.

We respect the decisions that parents or guardians make for their children. If you are not given

What happens if I see or experience something that confuses or concerns me when I’m using

We recommend that you share this information with a trusted adult at your school. This way， the adult
can support you with how to understand why the AI might “Hallucinate” or say something unrelated to
what you asked of it. Remember， generative AI is technology. Technology is not perfect and will make
mistakes.
In what ways can I use generative AI tools? Am I allowed to use it to help me with my work?
Houston ISD encourages students to use generative AI as a learning support tool to prepare for the
future workforce. When permitted by the teacher， AI may be used for activities such as brainstorming
ideas， organizing thoughts， conducting research， or receiving feedback.
AI may not be used to bypass learning， complete assignments dishonestly， or misrepresent original
work. In CTE courses， AI may support ideation， practice， simulation， and feedback， but it may not
replace hands-on skill demonstration， performance tasks， or certification-aligned assessments.

follow academic integrity expectations， including properly citing any AI-assisted content.
AI Guidebook // Frequently Asked Questions 20
Houston Independent School District
Frequently Asked Questions
Staff
How do I know which of my students has permission to access generative AI?
The Central Office team will manage student access to generative AI tools based on age and parental
consent. Additionally， each campus is responsible for keeping a record of parent permission decisions
granted for AI tool usage. Before a teacher brings generative AI into the classroom， please ensure
that you review student permission. If a student does not have permission to access generative AI
independently， you must ensure that the student can still participate in the learning and is not placed
at a disadvantage.
Do I have to use Microsoft Copilot Chat， Google Gemini， or ChatGPT Edu? Can I use generative AI
Chatbots that I’ve paid for myself to support my work?
We highly recommend our staff not use consumer chatbots for work-related activities. Sensitive data
is not protected in a way that complies with FERPA policy. For example， if you uploaded a data file
into your personal ChatGPT for analysis that includes student ID numbers and names， you have now
violated HISD Data privacy policies. Microsoft Copilot Chat， Google Gemini， and ChatGPT Edu reside
within the HISD domain and protects sensitive data. We trust that our employees will use their best
efforts to access the enterprise-level generative AI tools to support their efficiency and productivity in
a way that keeps district data private and secure.
Can I use generative AI tools outside of the approved list with my students?
We hope our staff continue to explore generative AI tools. And， we also know that we must take
great care and responsibility to put vetted products in front of our students. We highly recommend
teachers allow only students to use district approved AI tools， such as the preferred Google Gemini
or Microsoft Copilot Chat， if they are above the 8th grade or above and have parent permission. Even
with vetted tools， teachers must review images for appropriateness and accuracy before showing them
to students. For example， a teacher might ask a generative AI image creation tool to show a picture
of what a revolutionary war hospital might have looked like. Before embedding it into a lesson， the
teacher is responsible for checking the image for accuracy and suitability for the students.
Who can I talk to if an issue arises on my campus or in my department concerning a generative AI
tool?
It is our expectation that campus and central office staff will communicate openly about experiences
with generative AI tools. This landscape is new and consistently evolving. If you run into a concerning
situation， whereby the generative AI chatbot hallucinates or shares concerning or inaccurate content，
it is important to share that information with the AI Support Team. Instructions for how to connect
with that team can be found on page 19.
How is AI used in Houston ISD， and is it considered a system of record?
AI tools in Houston ISD are not systems of record and function only as professional planning and
drafting environments. All AI-assisted work is pre-decisional， requires human review， and any finalized
or official materials must be stored in HISD-approved systems (e.g.， email， SharePoint， OneDrive， SIS，
ERP).
AI Guidebook // Frequently Asked Questions 21
Houston Independent School District
Frequently Asked Questions
Families Are generative AI tools appropriate for my child， especially if they are 8th grade or above?
Generative AI tools have different age restrictions. At this time， Houston ISD will provide access to
Google Gemini to students， 8th grade and above who have obtained parental consent. The district will
prioritize responsible use training for both students and staff as well as support students if content is
returned that is inappropriate.
Is my student’s data protected while using generative AI tools?
Student data protection is a top priority in Houston ISD. If a student uses consumer-based AI tools
(such as public versions of ChatGPT) outside of district-managed platforms， any information entered
may be shared with the company that operates the tool.
Houston ISD provides access to secure， district-managed AI environments， including the enterprise
version of Google Gemini for staff and students ages 13 and older. These tools do not use student or
staff data to train external AI models and operate within HISD’s security and privacy requirements，
including access controls， monitoring， and safeguards designed to prevent the exposure or misuse of
sensitive information.
What if I have questions or concerns about how my student engages with generative AI tools?
With any new initiative， we expect our families to have questions about how their students might
engage with this new technology. A family should feel comfortable in reaching out to their child’s
teacher with questions. In addition， families can also submit concerns to the AI Support Team.
Instructions for how to connect with that team can be found on page 19.
If I do not give my student permission to access generative AI tools， are they able to still
engage in learning?
Yes. Houston ISD believes AI literacy is an important skill for Destination 2035， and we respect the
decisions families make regarding generative AI use. Students without parental consent will continue
to receive high-quality， equitable instruction without direct AI tool interaction， including alternative
learning opportunities as needed. Teachers may model AI use or provide AI-supported materials that
do not require individual student accounts， and no student will be disadvantaged academically or in
grading.

title: Policy 232.1 - Use of Artificial Intelligence (IDEA Public Schools)
full_text:
232.1 Use of Artificial Intelligence
The School is committed to supporting students and staff in the appropriate use of artificial
intelligence (“AI”). The use of AI technology is encouraged when used appropriately and ethically.
AI may be integrated into academic material responsibly to prepare students for the successful
integration of innovative technologies. The School will strive for the implementation of AI to be
human-centered and empower students and staff. If utilizing artificial intelligence technology，
students and staff shall abide by this policy and all relevant related policies.
Definitions
Artificial intelligence (AI): A machine-based system that can， for a given set of human-defined
objectives， make predictions， recommendations， or decisions influencing real or virtual
environments. Artificial intelligence systems use machine- and human-based inputs to perceive
real and virtual environments; abstract such perceptions into models through analysis in an
automated manner; and use model inference to formulate options for information or action.
Generative AI: Any internet-based generative artificial intelligence programs that make use of
large language model algorithms to make something new. AI used for auto-complete， minor text
predictions， and/or grammar/spelling/punctuation suggestions， commonly found in most word-
processing applications， is not considered generative AI.
AI tool: AI applications， algorithms， or systems that make use of AI to generate outputs based on
human inputs， with an emphasis on generative AI.
Data Privacy
The School is committed to protecting student and staff data consistent with state and federal laws
and regulations. The use of AI shall adhere to existing data privacy policies including， but not
limited to， policies related to the release of student records and information (see Policy 294).
Procurement of AI Tools
The adoption and use of AI tools shall be in accordance with the School’s procurement policies
and in alignment with the School’s mission. All AI technologies provided by vendors shall adhere
to the School’s policies and current state and federal laws and regulations.
Acceptable Use of AI
It is understood that all students and staff may use AI technology from time-to-time on School
grounds; provided however， AI shall always be used in a manner appropriate to the School’s
academic and moral goals， and is only permissible to be used in the academic setting when
authorized by the classroom instructor. Failure to use AI technology in an appropriate manner may
subject students and staff to disciplinary action.
Artificial Intelligence Technology may not be utilized for the following:
1. Violating the conditions of federal and Ohio law dealing with students’ and employees’
rights to privacy;
2. Creating images which may be offensive to another user; bullying， insulting， intimidating，
or attacking others; or transmitting any material in violation of federal or state law.
3. Accessing or creating profanity， obscenity， abusive， pornographic， and/ or impolite
language or materials; accessing materials in violation of the Student Code of Conduct; or
viewing， creating， or accessing materials that you would not want instructors and parents
to see. Should a student encounter any inappropriate materials by accident， he/she should
report it to his or her instructors immediately.
4. Violating copyright laws by utilizing copyrighted images. All copyright laws must be
respected.
5. Plagiarizing works through AI Technology. Plagiarism is taking ideas of others and
presenting them as if they were original to the user. While AI Technology may be used to
support a student’s learning， AI generated work shall not replace a student’s work.
6. Damaging Technology devices， computers， computer systems， or computer networks (for
example， by the creation， introduction， or spreading of computer viruses， physically
abusing hardware， altering source codes or software settings， etc.).
7. Using the Technology or the Internet for commercial purposes or activities， which are
defined as offering or providing goods or services or purchasing goods or services for
personal use， and include， but are not limited to， the following:
a. any activity that requires an exchange of money and/or credit card numbers;
b. any activity that requires entry into an area of service for which the School will be
charged a fee;
c. any purchase or sale of any kind; or
d. any use for product advertisement or political lobbying.
8. Using AI for any purpose which is illegal or against the School’s policies or contrary to the
School’s mission or best interests.
R.C. 3301.24; 15 U.S.C. Section 9401
See also Policy 204.16 Cyber Threats; Policy 232 Technology and Internet Acceptable Use; Policy
271 Student Code of Conduct; Policy 294 Student Records and Release of Information; Policy
397.2 Acceptable Uses of the School’s Equipment; 397.3 Unacceptable Uses of the School’s
Equipment.
CERTIFICATION
The Undersigned， being the Board President， hereby certifies that the foregoing represents a true
copy of the Board Policy relating to the Use of Artificial Intelligence policy， as originally adopted
by the Board on April 20， 2026， which Policy， is in full force and effect and has not been revoked
or amended.

Artificial Intelligence
Artificial Intelligence， specifically Generative AI (Gen AI)， is a technology tool that can be trained to think and learn like humans. It has the potential to augment teaching and learning by streamlining administrative tasks， calculating data， running simulations， and refining project development as a thought partner. The capabilities of these technologies also necessitate careful guidance to ensure responsible and equitable usage. Fort Bend ISD (FBISD) recognizes the importance of establishing clear guidelines and best practices around Gen AI integration in the educational setting.
The primary goal of the guidelines is to inform students， staff， and stakeholders of the responsible and ethical use of Gen AI and its use with other technology tools. Although Gen AI may be able to create， revise， or complete tasks quickly， the amplification of learning is the primary outcome.

Board CQC (LOCAL) Administrative Regulations
ARGYLE ISD ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE GUIDELINES
The Texas Education Agency (TEA) does not enforce a single state-mandated policy on student
use of artificial intelligence. Instead， the TEA leaves specific AI adoption， guardrails， and student
usage rules up to individual local school districts. The Texas Education Agency does use AI
directly to automate the scoring of written responses on STAAR tests.
Argyle ISD Board Policy CQD (LOCAL) states: Employees and students shall be permitted to explore
AI and implement its use in and out of the classroom in accordance with policy and administrative
regulations. The use of AI shall only be as a support tool to enhance student outcomes and shall never
take the place of teacher and student decision-making. Any use of AI must comply with law， policy， and
administrative regulations relating to student and employee privacy and data security. A student shall
only use AI tools with teacher permission and shall be expected to produce original work and properly
credit sources， including AI tools used in creating the work. Students who use AI tools to deceptively
harm， bully， or harass others shall be disciplined in accordance with the Student Code of Conduct and
policy. [See EIA(LOCAL)， FFH， FFI， and the FO series]
In her Dear Colleague Letter on the use of artificial intelligence in education， Secretary Linda
McMahon outlined five principles for the responsible use of AI: education technologies should be
educator-led， ethical， accessible， transparent， and protective of student data. These principles provide a
strong foundation not only for artificial intelligence but for educational technology more broadly.
The accompanying Administrative Regulations for CDQ (LOCAL) outline the technology
standards for artificial intelligence (AI) regarding academic integrity and operational use:
ACADEMIC INTEGRITY: These regulations outline guidelines and principles for the
responsible and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in educational settings.
Argyle ISD is committed to academic integrity by fostering a culture of originality and
creativity and placing a strong emphasis on ethical practices. We recognize the potential of
AI tools to enrich and support learning experiences. However， we strictly prohibit the use
of AI to commit authorship fraud. Argyle ISD believes in the importance of individual
effort， critical thinking， and the responsible use of all technology.
Teachers play a crucial role in educating students about the appropriate use of AI tools，
including their strengths and weaknesses， to optimize their value in the learning process.
Educators will provide guidelines on the sanctionable use of AI in their classroom and on
individual assignments.
We emphasize the following expectations regarding the use of AI tools in student
assignments:
1. Originality: Students must take personal responsibility for the originality and
authorship of their work. Assignments should reflect their own thoughts， ideas，
and understanding of the subject matter.
2. Citation: When incorporating AI-generated content into their assignments，
students must acknowledge its use and accurately cite and attribute the sources.
3. Integrity: Students should adhere to the principles of academic integrity and
honesty. Plagiarism， whether facilitated by AI tools or any other means， is strictly
prohibited.
Artificial intelligence may never replace a student's own thinking or learning.
Unauthorized AI use—including using AI during quizzes， tests， or other assessments， or
submitting AI-generated work as original work—constitutes academic dishonesty and will
be addressed in accordance with the Student Code of Conduct. Consequences may include，
but are not limited to， revision of assignments， loss of assignment credit， parental
involvement， or other appropriate measures deemed necessary by the school
administration.
By upholding these guidelines， we commit to fostering a safe， responsible environment
that promotes ethical practices and academic integrity， and that prepares the next
generation for the challenges and opportunities of AI technology.
OPERATIONAL USE: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a tool designed to support learning
and productivity—not replace the critical thinking， creativity， and meaningful relationships that
define the Argyle ISD learning experience. Our approach to AI will remain thoughtful，
age-appropriate， and aligned with our commitment to Hands-On， Minds-On Learning.
Employee Use
District employees may use AI tools to enhance instructional planning， professional
responsibilities， and operational efficiency， while maintaining student privacy and confidentiality
and complying with District policy. Employees remain responsible for all instructional decisions，
the accuracy of AI-assisted content， and the protection of confidential or personally identifiable
student information.
Student Use
Grades PK–8
● Students will not use generative AI for classroom assignments， projects， research， or
homework.
● Instruction will emphasize foundational skills， critical thinking， problem solving，
collaboration， and authentic student work.
● Exception for District-adopted instructional materials:
○ Students may use Argyle ISD's adopted HMH curriculum， which includes Writable，
an instructional writing platform that uses AI to provide feedback during the
writing process. When used as part of classroom instruction under a teacher's
guidance， Writable serves as an instructional support tool to strengthen students'
writing and revision skills. Its use within the adopted curriculum is permitted and
is not considered student use of generative AI under these procedures.
○ Students may use Argyle ISD's adopted HMH curriculum resource， Amira， an
AI-powered reading tutor used for personalized reading intervention. Amira is a
resource for supporting student growth.
Grades 9–12
● Students may use Argyle ISD's adopted HMH curriculum， which includes Writable， an
instructional writing platform that uses AI to provide feedback during the writing
process.
● Students may use generative AI only when specifically authorized by the classroom
teacher for an identified instructional purpose.
● When AI is permitted， students must disclose its use， evaluate the accuracy and reliability
of AI-generated information， and remain responsible for the originality and quality of all
work submitted.

AI CODE OF ETHICS AND MINIMUM STANDARDS:

INTRODUCTION
This guidebook supports students， families， and staff in building AI literacy and using GenAI safely， responsibly， and effectively. As AI technologies continue to evolve， this guidebook will be updated to reflect emerging tools， best practices， and changing educational needs.
What is AI and GenAI?
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science focused on building machines that mimic human intelligence. It generally falls into two main categories:
Predictive (Traditional) AI:
Analyzes existing data to recognize patterns， make choices， or predict outcomes.
Examples: Movie recommendations， auto-correct， and digital assistants (Siri/Alexa).
Generative AI (GenAI):
Processes massive datasets to create entirely new， original content.
Examples: Generating new text， images， code， or audio (ChatGPT， Gemini).
Our Why
PSJA ISD's commitment to
College³ - Ready. Connected. Complete.
calls us to equip every learner with the knowledge， skills， and character needed to thrive in an AI-enabled world.
Learners
AI serves as a catalyst to enrich instruction， promote equity， and prepare graduates for future-ready success.
For Our Educators
AI is a tool to increase productivity and elevate professional practice while keeping human connection at the center of the classroom.
GUIDING PRINCIPLES
Adapted from AI guidance for schools toolkit， by TeachAI， 2025 (https://www.teachai.org/toolkit). Copyright 2025 by TeachAI.
Putting People First
AI empowers teachers and students， keeping humans in control. Humans retain ultimate responsibility for all decisions and outcomes.
Upholding Learning with Integrity
AI is a partner in ethical and transparent learning. Students use AI ethically and transparently to spark ideas and deepen understanding.
Cultivating Future-Ready Growth
Preparing students for an AI-integrated world. We build AI literacy by teaching students how AI works， how to use it responsibly， and how to evaluate its output to ensure success in college， careers， and life.
Safeguarding Safety and Privacy
Protecting student data and identity. We strictly select and utilize AI tools that meet rigorous data privacy and digital footprint standards.
Advancing Fair and Equal Access
Prioritizing fair and equal access to ensure all students have access to AI tools. We provide equitable access to high-quality tools that meet diverse learning needs and help every student reach their full potential.
Prioritizing Active Monitoring
Regularly reviewing AI use for effectiveness and safety. We evaluate AI tools and monitor school usage to ensure that these technologies always enhance learning， protect users， and uphold high ethical standards.
PRIVACY & SECURITY
To safeguard student privacy， ensure instructional integrity， and boost professional productivity， please follow these guidelines for district-approved AI tools (accessible via your district login). Do not use non-approved AI resources for any work-related activities.
Student Privacy & Data Protection (FERPA Compliance)
In accordance with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) and PSJA ISD Board Policy FL (LEGAL)， safeguarding student data is a critical legal requirement.
STOP: Under no circumstances should staff enter， upload， paste， or describe identifiable student information into public AI tools or prompts.
Treat prompts as data leaving district systems. Even partial information combined with context can make a student identifiable.
Examples of Strictly Prohibited Information:
Basic Identifiers:
Student names (first and last)， Student ID numbers， dates of birth， home addresses， or parent/guardian names.
Protected Records:
Social Security numbers， disciplinary records， health/medical information， or human resources/payroll info.
Academic & Support Data:
Grades connected to an identifiable student， or Special Education (IEP) and Section 504 details tied to a specific student.
Incident Reporting Protocol
If you suspect a data exposure， a security breach， or the misuse of an AI tool， you must report it immediately to mitigate data risk.
Report to:
PSJA ISD IT Helpdesk
Submission Channels:
Helpdesk Portal Link
|
helpdesk@psjaisd.us
STAFF AI EXPECTATIONS
Personal AI Account Policy
While PSJA ISD requires district-managed credentials for standard work to ensure legal compliance (CIPA， COPPA， FERPA， PPRA)， it recognizes that staff may use personal premium accounts (e.g.， ChatGPT Plus， Gemini Advanced) for advanced features. When doing so， staff must strictly adhere to data privacy guardrails: never enter student Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or confidential district data into an AI account.
Staff Security Protocols
To ensure network security and data loss prevention， all staff members must adhere to the following operational guardrails:
District-Managed Accounts Only:
Always log in using official PSJA ISD Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace credentials. Never use personal emails or accounts for district business.
Approved Storage Systems:
Store and share district documents only within approved environments (Google Drive， SharePoint， OneDrive， Teams). Follow all existing sharing and permission rules.
No Unapproved Add-ons:
Do not install AI browser extensions， add-ons， or connectors (for Google Workspace or Office 365) without explicit IT administrative approval.
Third-Party App Restriction:
Staff are prohibited from authorizing third-party apps or granting AI tools permission to access district accounts and data sets.
Managed Endpoints Only:
If an authorized AI tool requires file uploads or document access， it must only be accessed on managed district devices equipped with active endpoint protection.
Basic Identifiers:
Passwords， access tokens， or any login credentials for district-managed systems must never be shared into AI tools.
Always follow district guidelines for safe， responsible， and effective use of AI.
District Approved AI Tools
Information Technology Department maintains a vetted list of AI domains and applications. AI tools and related web traffic will be actively logged and inappropriate content will be blocked on district networks and managed devices.
Approved Tools Include:
ChatGPT， Microsoft Copilot， Gemini， MagicSchool AI， NotebookLM， Wayground， Khanmigo， Canva AI， Adobe Express， Diffit， Brisk， Curipod， TeachShare.
New tools for consideration must be requested and approved by the Information Technology Department (Send Requests to:
PSJA ISD IT Helpdesk
|
helpdesk@psjaisd.us
).
Before using any AI tool， confirm:
You are using a district-approved AI tool and a district-managed account.
No passwords， access tokens， or login credentials are included.
No student-identifiable information is included.
No confidential staff information is included.
Output has been fact-checked.
Content aligns with TEKS and district curriculum.
You have reviewed and edited the response.
Follow all Communications Department Guidelines on use of district branding.
STUDENT AI EXPECTATIONS
To ensure every PSJA ISD student is prepared to participate， compete， and excel in a global society， the district has established clear guidelines for student engagement with Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI).
Student AI Commitments
LEADER
I act honestly and practice good digital citizenship in all my interactions.
CHANGE AGENT
I learn and adjust to new tools and keep growing in a changing world.
VISIONARY IMPLEMENTER
I think critically， create original work and innovate with AI.
COMMUNITY DEVELOPER
I use AI to collaborate respectfully and make a positive impact on my community.
PSJA Student AI Quick Guide
You are the Pilot. AI is the Co-Pilot. Humans in the Lead.
You are responsible for your work and must verify all AI-generated output for accuracy.
DO
DON'T
Ask permission
Cite all use
Fact-check everything
No private info (ID， name， address)
No copy & paste
No cyberbullying
The Privacy Shield:
Never enter your Full Name， Student ID， or Home Address into an AI tool.
ACADEMIC INTEGRITY
Students must always ensure they have explicit permission from their teacher before utilizing Generative AI tools for any coursework. When used， its assistance must be openly disclosed with proper attribution.
Activities requiring disclosure or citation include:
Quoting， paraphrasing， or summarizing text generated by AI.
Incorporating AI-generated images， graphics， video， or audio into projects.
Using AI for brainstorming， structuring outlines， conducting preliminary research， or proofreading/editing drafts.
HOW TO ATTRIBUTE GEN AI USAGE
The type and depth of citation required depend entirely on the assignment and the teacher's expectations:
Formal Assignments (Essays， Research Papers):
Require a full bibliographic citation (such as MLA or APA) in the Works Cited or References list， alongside in-text citations.
Informal Assignments (Presentations， Group Projects， Short Writing):
Require a simple disclosure statement detailing how the AI was used.
SAMPLE CITATION (MLA FORMAT)
Format: Prompt， name of tool， version of tool， company， date of generation， general URL of tool
”Can you explain the difference between mitosis and meiosis using a simple sports analogy? Please don't give me a long essay; just break it down into bullet points.” ChatGPT， 4， June 2026， https://chatgpt.com.
SAMPLE DISCLOSURE OF AI USE
The sample disclosure might be used at the beginning， or at the end， of an AI-enhanced document:
Brainstormed ideas and narrowed down topic using Gemini
Asked for an analogy to better understand using ChatGPT
Edited and proofread final draft using Gemini
CITING TEXT & IMAGES
Cite text and images in presentations with a note naming the tool and prompt used， as well as the year.
Image generated with Gemini using the prompt ”duck on a pond，” 2026
For more details on MLA citation with AI:
https://style.mla.org/citing-generative-ai/
For more information on APA citation with AI:
https://apastyle.apa.org/blog/how-to-cite-chatgpt
USING AI RESPONSIBLY: EXAMPLES OF MISUSE
The following behaviors are considered inappropriate and may result in disciplinary action depending on severity and intent:
Academic Dishonesty / Plagiarism:
Using AI to generate essays， responses， or projects without teacher permission or failing to cite AI assistance when required.
Cheating on Assessments:
Using AI tools during quizzes， tests， or exams to obtain answers or complete work dishonestly.
Cyberbullying or Harassment:
Using AI to generate harmful messages， impersonate individuals， or target students or staff with offensive content.
Deepfakes or Manipulated Media:
Creating or sharing AI-generated images， videos， or audio intended to mislead， embarrass， or deceive others.
Inappropriate or Explicit Content Generation:
Using AI tools to produce violent， sexual， or otherwise inappropriate material.
Privacy Violations:
Entering or sharing personal， confidential， or sensitive information about self or others into AI platforms without authorization.
Security Violations / Hacking Attempts:
Using AI to attempt unauthorized access to school systems， accounts， or restricted data.
Misinformation and Disinformation:
Using AI to generate or distribute false or misleading information that could disrupt school operations or harm individuals or the school community.
When students are uncertain about appropriate AI use， they are expected to seek guidance from teachers， counselors， or campus administrators.
STOP: Misuse of AI tools is considered a violation of the PSJA ISD Student Code of Conduct and will be addressed in alignment with district disciplinary procedures and campus-level implementation guidance.

Artificial Intelligence in Celina ISD
Vision Statement for Artificial Intelligence Integration
Celina ISD will intentionally integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a catalyst for learning， creativity， and efficiency， empowering students and educators to deepen understanding， expand ideas， and work more effectively.
Grounded in the belief that education is fundamentally human， we will ensure AI enhances critical thinking， originality， and the productive struggle essential to meaningful learning. AI will serve as a tool for research， clarification， and the expansion of existing ideas， supporting both instruction and efficiency without diminishing authentic thinking.
Through comprehensive training， clear guidelines， and ethical guardrails， we will equip our learners to use AI responsibly， embracing innovation while maintaining academic integrity and personal responsibility. By focusing on strategic implementation， we will prepare students to confidently navigate and shape a future where AI enhances opportunity， fosters innovation， and amplifies human potential.
Love the learner; drive the rigor
We believe the effective use of AI should help us know every learner deeply， meet their individual needs， and expand opportunities for growth.
AI supports personalization， accessibility， and engagement while also elevating expectations through inquiry， critical thinking， and enriched learning experiences.
Responsible for one own learning
We believe the effective use of AI should empower ownership of learning through ethical use， reflection， and independent thinking.
AI is a tool that helps learners plan and evaluate information， build skills， and demonstrate integrity in their academic work.
Interdependent self-managers
We believe the effective use of AI should strengthen the ability to collaborate， set goals， manage tasks， and maintain accountability.
AI supports planning， metacognition， and productive teamwork while reinforcing the need for shared responsibility and meaningful human collaboration.
How are teachers using AI to teach?
Is AI safe to use in the classroom?
What AI does my child have access to?
How do teachers prevent students from misusing AI?
Is AI use appropriate for all grade levels?
What policies are in place for AI use?
The foundation of our instructional practices are grounded in the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS). Our district has invested significant time， careful consideration， and financial resources into selecting and providing High-Quality Instructional Materials (HQIM) that support a rigorous， guaranteed， and viable education for our students. Artificial Intelligence is a powerful tool available to enhance and support the implementation of our instructional practices.
When used responsibly， Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be a safe and valuable tool for learning. Our district only allows the use of AI systems that meet strict safety， privacy， and educational standards. Additionally， all approved resource providers are required to sign our DPA (Data Privacy Agreement). Any AI tools used in our classrooms must comply with federal and state student privacy laws， including:
FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act): protects the privacy of student education records
COPPA (Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act): applies to online services used by children under 13
Texas student data privacy laws: provides additional safeguards around how student data is collected and used
Our district provides students with access to carefully selected， school-approved tools that include Artificial Intelligence features to support learning. We currently provide access to MagicSchool， an AI-powered platform designed specifically for education. It is used in structured， teacher-guided ways to support student learning.
In addition， some of the digital tools our students already use include built-in AI features， such as writing support， feedback， or tutoring assistance. These features are part of platforms that have been reviewed and approved by the district.
Teachers use a combination of clear expectations， thoughtful assignment design， and active monitoring to ensure Artificial Intelligence (AI) is used appropriately， not as a shortcut. Students are given specific expectations for when and how AI can be used. Just like other tools， using AI in ways that violate assignment guidelines is considered academic dishonesty as addressed in the Celina ISD Student Handbook.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) use is always determined by what is developmentally appropriate. Teachers adjust how AI is used based on student maturity， skill level， and the learning goals of the lesson. AI can be appropriate at all grade levels when used thoughtfully， starting with strong teacher guidance in early grades and gradually building toward responsible， independent use as students develop.
All guardians must agree annually to the Celina ISD Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) as defined in CQ(Local). The following Artificial Intelligence clarification is included in the AUP:
The use of AI technology in the PK-12 school district must comply with the district's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP). AI technology can be an excellent resource for enhancing learning and teaching experiences， but it must be used responsibly and ethically. Students， teachers， and staff members must ensure that any AI systems they use are age-appropriate and that they do not violate the privacy of other individuals. The use of AI for academic purposes should align with the district's curriculum and instruction goals. Additionally， students， teachers， and staff must use AI tools responsibly， avoiding any form of plagiarism or cheating. Failure to follow these guidelines may result in disciplinary action， including suspension or revocation of access to AI technology. By following these guidelines， we can ensure that AI technology is used appropriately and safely within the PK-12 school district.

How does Plano ISD support responsible， open and future-ready use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and what steps are taken to ensure students and staff are prepared to use these technologies effectively and ethically?
AI is incorporated into many tools available to Plano ISD staff and students.  Notably， as part of our Microsoft 365 A5 Education License， we have access to Copilot Chat.  Similarly， under an educational licensing agreement with Google， we have access to Gemini and NotebookLM.  Additionally， there are some generative AI capabilities embedded into a range of other tools we offer like Adobe Express and Canva.  For students， it is important to note that these tools must only be used with teacher approval.  And even when AI tools are used， we expect such use to be transparent:  students and teachers should talk openly about how AI was used in assignments and for what purpose(s).
Approved general-purpose AI tools are posted on our Approved Apps Portal
here
.  There are other approved applications that contain AI-enhanced features (e.g. Adobe Express， Canva， etc).  All approved applications are posted
